claims.subject: gatewatch

evidence.quote: Five Planeswalkers have come to Amonkhet to slay a dragon.
the dragon Planeswalker Nicol Bolas was perhaps the greatest such threat. So they came to Amonkhet

claims.summary: The five Gatewatch members come to Amonkhet to slay Nicol Bolas.

claims.subject: nicol_bolas

evidence.quote: the twin curving horns of Nicol Bolas—the so-called God-Pharaoh—stood as a reminder of Gideon's purpose here
"Hail, Nicol Bolas, God-Pharaoh of Amonkhet!"

claims.summary: On Amonkhet Nicol Bolas is the God-Pharaoh.

claims.subject: nicol_bolas

evidence.quote: Nissa discovered hints of Amonkhet's past, a history Nicol Bolas has overwritten.

claims.summary: Bolas has overwritten Amonkhet's past (official recap).

claims.subject: liliana_vess

evidence.quote: She came to the plane to find—and kill—another of her demon creditors.

claims.summary: Liliana came to Amonkhet to kill another of her demon creditors.

claims.subject: liliana_vess

evidence.quote: "I killed Kothophed and Griselbrand," Liliana replied with a ghost of a smile.

claims.summary: Liliana says she has already killed Kothophed and Griselbrand.
claims.limitation: Liliana's own statement to Razaketh; the killings happened in earlier arcs and are not narrated here.

claims.subject: liliana_vess

evidence.quote: Without hesitation or humanity, her two dozen selves consumed the last of the demon Razaketh.

claims.summary: Through two dozen undead crocodiles, Liliana devours the demon Razaketh.

claims.subject: kefnet

evidence.quote: Now she seeks answers from the God of Knowledge, hoping Kefnet can explain the veneer that seems to obscure the plane.

claims.summary: Kefnet is Amonkhet's God of Knowledge.

claims.subject: nicol_bolas

evidence.quote: The God-Pharaoh has returned, and the five Hours have arrived as foretold.

claims.summary: The God-Pharaoh returns and the five Hours arrive (official recap).

claims.subject: bontu

evidence.quote: Bontu strode forward and knelt in supplication to the God-Pharaoh.

claims.summary: Bontu kneels to Bolas as the God-Pharaoh.

claims.subject: hazoret

evidence.quote: The name Bontu had uttered—Nicol Bolas—had sent another searing pain through Hazoret's head, and she was now certain: some magic was suppressing her memories.

claims.summary: The name Nicol Bolas pains Hazoret, who realises magic is suppressing her memories.
claims.limitation: Hazoret concludes that some magic suppresses her memories; the text does not here say Bolas cast it.

claims.subject: nicol_bolas

evidence.quote: "No, master, I did not doubt. I was . . . delayed. You defeated them as quickly as you predicted."
The planar bridge was his. The army was ready. The Gatewatch was loose in the Multiverse.

claims.summary: Bolas defeats the Gatewatch on Amonkhet; the survivors scatter into the Multiverse.

claims.subject: chandra_nalaar

evidence.quote: Chandra couldn't find Gideon. She couldn't save Nissa. She couldn't beat the dragon.
She planeswalked away in a fiery blaze, the only trace left of her presence the blood that stained the broken rocks as it, too, evaporated under the fiery heat.

claims.summary: Chandra planeswalks away from the losing fight.

claims.subject: gideon_jura

evidence.quote: Bolas did not think Gideon's choice mattered. In the end, it was the dragon's indifference that settled his choice.
He willed his body through the Blind Eternities, the hole the dragon left in his shoulder only the most visible of his wounds.

claims.summary: Wounded, Gideon leaves Amonkhet through the Blind Eternities.

claims.subject: tezzeret

evidence.quote: Tezzeret had served him long enough to know the right answer.

claims.summary: Tezzeret arrives on Amonkhet as Bolas's servant.

claims.subject: nicol_bolas

evidence.quote: The planar bridge was his. The army was ready.

claims.summary: Bolas now has the Planar Bridge and an army ready (the Amonkhet Eternals, per later arcs).
claims.limitation: The 'army' is not named in this quote; identifying it with the Eternals is left to later packs.

claims.subject: nicol_bolas

evidence.quote: "Later. Go and tell Ral Zarek to come to me. His progress is too slow."

claims.summary: Bolas sends Tezzeret to fetch Ral Zarek, whose (unnamed) work is too slow, foreshadowing War of the Spark.

claims.subject: nicol_bolas

evidence.quote: Several decades ago he had come to the world of Amonkhet, a blighted, superstitious backworld of interest to no one who mattered
He had wrought well in his creation sixty years ago.

claims.summary: Bolas came to Amonkhet decades before the story and shaped its present order around sixty years earlier.
claims.limitation: 'Several decades' and 'sixty years ago' are Bolas's point-of-view narration relative to the story; kept as relative dates, not absolute years.

remaining: Writing on the Wall, Brazen, Judgment, Hour of Revelation/Glory/Promise and Endure episodes are uncited
Trespass (Samut/Djeru/Hapatra backstory) is not modelled yet
Gods' deaths (Oketra, Kefnet, Rhonas) and Samut's spark are not yet modelled
